originality.rationale: The structural classification of both equality families was already known and is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim (Polcyn-Rucinski Theorem 2 and Theorem 4(ii); Kostochka-Mubayi Section 1). The proposed new theorem constructs and identifies an optimal-state batch-exchange graph by complete pair-overlap comparisons and proves the sharp linear movement threshold and constant global eccentricity. Targeted exact/alias searches found no covering graph theorem. The indexed small-n diversity result is distinct. Publication-priority uncertainty remains for unindexed or differently formulated results.

value.rationale: Unlike the known extremal family counts, the theorem answers natural optimal-preserving reconfiguration questions: linear-size frozen barrier r<n-4, exact first-mobility graph, uniform regularity and global radius/diameter five despite growing ground set. This reveals cross-type hub transitions between n Johnson layers. Such geometric mobility is potentially useful for stability and constrained switching of extremal triple systems. Scope is natural, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
